The diagram shown above is the slope field for which of the following differential equations?
worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14069384/assets/3b77cdfa4958cd1892c31baf858b5f8cbe29e00e8e2a45b698a43c5ddae6198e.png)

 

Notice the following properties of the given slope field:

- First, the slopes of the slope field are horizontal along the line $y=0,$ as shown above. Therefore, the right-hand side of the differential equation should evaluate to zero on this line.

Of the given equations, the only equations that satisfy this condition are the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =y \\ {y}^{′} & ={y}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

- Second, the line $y=0$ divide the plane into $2$ regions. The sign of the slopes in each of the $2$ regions are easily deduced by considering the behavior of the solution curves in these regions. This information is summarized in the following table:

| $y>0$ | $↗$

$(+)$ |
| --- | --- |
| $y<0$ | $↘$

$(-)$ |

Of the remaining options, the only one that gives this behavior is

$$
{y}^{′}=y.
$$
